ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 7330, as most recently amended), including its Presidential Enforcement Decree and the Financial Services Commission/KoFIU reporting regulations; Act on Prohibition of Financing of Offenses Affecting Public Interest; Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; Commercial Registration Act; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; and the FATF standards implemented through KoFIU supervisory guidance. For a Yuhan Hoesa, beneficial ownership must be collected and held at government-only access level by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, licensed banking institutions, and the corporate registry record, without public inspection.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Corporate Registration Certificate of the Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, District Court Registry Office at the registered seat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: obtain certified registration extract from the court registry; notarize the registry officer's signature if required; obtain an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; file directly with the receiving registry or banking institution. Consular Legalization route, available only if the receiving jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member: obtain certified court extract; authenticate it through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; then legalize at the relevant embassy or consulate of the receiving jurisdiction. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: certified extract from the court registry, ministerial apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, direct use. Consular Legalization route, only for non-member states: certified extract, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then legalization by the receiving state's diplomatic post. Never sequentially combine apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation agents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The incorporators and directors of the Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: sign before Korean notary public, then obtain Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular route, only for non-member states: sign before notary, authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the consulate of the destination jurisdiction. Either route is chosen solely based on the destination state's membership in the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified copy of the constitutional instrument of the Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea or the notary public who authenticated the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: certified copy from the court registry or notary's original, then Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route, only for non-member states: certified copy or notary original, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then legalization by the destination state's consulate. Parallel paths only; no sequential chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and AML/KYC Customer Due Diligence Confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed Korean commercial bank maintaining or opening the corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: bank officer signs before a notary, notarization, and Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular Legalization route, only for non-member states: same notarization, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and consular legalization by the receiving state. Apostille and consular legalization remain mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of corporate registration or Korean notary public maintaining the seal registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: notarized seal imprint certificate, Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, direct acceptance. For non-Apostille states: notarized seal certificate, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then consular legalization. Do not apply both processes to a single certificate.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all directors, legal representatives, ultimate beneficial owners at the 25% threshold, shareholders, authorized signatories, and beneficial holders' immediate family and close associates. Screening must be run against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit designated lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions, United States Office of Foreign Assets Control SDN and non-SDN Sectoral Sanctions, EU and UK consolidated lists, and Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and National Security Act designated individual lists. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for any politically exposed person, adverse media, sanctions hit, high-risk jurisdiction nexus, or unusual source-of-funds information. The compliance review must be documented and approved by the AML compliance officer before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (IRO) - Corporate Registration name clearance and search module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Korean company name must be expressed in Hangul for registration. A parallel English or romanized trade name may be used for invoices and contracts only if the Hangul name is registered and the foreign name is transliterated consistently. The name must include the legal form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' for a limited liability company. Four-tier naming governance requires evaluation of the Hangul text, the romanized transliteration, the use of foreign original-language words, and the corporate designator, so that no identical or deceptively similar name exists among companies with the same business scope in the same registration district.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: and other terms reserved by relevant Korean licensing statutes
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, request a written statement of the statutory ground and re-check the registry record. File a correction or objection with the District Court Registry Office within 14 days, attaching the original name search report, a revised Hangul name with transliteration, and, if applicable, written consent or ministerial authorization from the Ministry of the Interior and Safety or the relevant supervisory authority. If the court registry maintains the rejection, petition the district court for administrative adjudication under the Administrative Litigation Act; if that fails, file an appeal to the appellate division within 30 days of service, retaining counsel for the hearing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa engaged in publishing simulated social casino and virtual slots games, a bare mailing address, virtual mailbox, or shared address with no physical operations will be treated critically by the National Tax Service, local tax offices, and bank AML departments. A serviced office with a dedicated lease, floor and unit specific address, physical signage, onboarding of an employee or agent during business hours, access to books and records, and a genuine business telephone line may be acceptable. However, Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant registrations, as well as Korean banks, often require the entity to appear on the payment gateway's records with a verifiable physical address and a utility bill in the company's name. A full virtual office is therefore permissible only as a transitional sales-support office; the statutory head office must retain substantive administration and cannot be outsourced to a mail-forwarding company.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection likelihood is 30% within the first 12 months and 55% within 36 months for a newly incorporated digital-content company using a non-traditional head office. Checklist for inspectors: exact floor and unit visible on the door and lease; corporate nameplate posted outside the office; original articles, minutes, books, and seal available or retrievable within 24 hours; utility and telecommunication invoices addressed to the head office; an employee or office manager physically present; business registration certificate displayed or readily available; no PO Box, personal residence, or mail forwarder; server and operations logs accessible if requested. Registry, municipal, and tax inspection risk becomes low when all checklist items are satisfied.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Book IV, Part V concerning Yuhan Hoesa (Articles 553 through 583), together with Articles 288, 289, 290, 295, 317, 318, 376, 382, 393, 423, 448 and 543 concerning incorporation procedure, capital subscription, registration, directors' authority and corporate governance; Foreign Investment Promotion Act is supplementary only where capital is invested by non-resident shareholders and FDI benefits are sought.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division (Registry Office) of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operating under the Superintendence of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea through the InterNet Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa, comprising the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital subscription and deposit certificates, consents of directors and auditor, and corporate seal registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None mandatory by the Commercial Act; a Yuhan Hoesa may be formed with any positive paid-in capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation. No blocked escrow account is required for local formation; capital must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate in the corporate name before registration. If foreign-invested status under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act is desired, a minimum investment of KRW 100,000,000 or the relevant converted amount and a foreign investment report to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or KOTRA may apply, but this is not a registration prerequisite for a purely domestic company. Court registration fees vary with declared capital; no part is treated as a statutory capital escrow.

The Board considered the incorporation records, the subscription statement, the bank deposit certificate, and the draft Articles. After discussion, the Board unanimously adopted the following resolutions effective immediately. 1. Share Capital Subscription. Withdrawals exceeding [•] Korean won require two authorized signatories. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board approved and adopted the premises located at [•], Republic of Korea, as the registered office and head office, and directed the Representative Director to execute the office lease, file the registration of the registered office with the competent Registry Office, notify the National Tax Service, and obtain the building occupancy and fire safety documents required for the leased premises. 4. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: InterNet Registry of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea and the Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator or its licensed attorney prepares and submits a nationwide corporate name search for the proposed Korean legal name of the Yuhan Hoesa, including the entity suffix and the software publishing purpose. At least two alternative names should be submitted because the Registry will reject a proposed name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, or that contains a prohibited or misleading expression. The searcher must record the submitted name, the search result, and the expiration date of any reservation. If the name is available, the reservation letter is placed in the legal dossier and used as a supporting document for the later registration filing.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the incorporator or authorized representative
Proposed Articles of Incorporation draft showing purpose clause
First, second and third chosen Korean company name variants
Power of attorney if filing through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, the attorney immediately files a revised application using the pre-selected alternative name and corrects the purpose clause; no new payment is required unless the existing reservation is already exhausted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Capital Subscription and Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Korea selected by the incorporators; notary public for optional notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After confirmation of the corporate name and finalization of the Articles, the incorporators open a temporary share subscription account at a Korean commercial bank and deposit the paid-in capital. The bank issues a deposit certificate identifying the company, the subscribers and the amount paid. The incorporators then subscribe all shares by executing subscription statements and signing the Articles of Incorporation. Where the Articles require or the legal counsel recommends notarization, the incorporators appear before a Korean notary to certify the signatures and the fact of incorporation consent. The subscription statements, deposit certificate, and notarized Articles are compiled into a certified capital-payment package which is later delivered to the Registry Office.
required_dossiers: Final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Subscription statement signed by each incorporator
Certificate of paid-in capital issued by the bank
Corporate seal specimen and application for seal registration
Identity documents of all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is rejected for containing errors or insufficient subscriber identification, the bank reissues a corrected certificate after re-verifying identity; if a subscriber defaults, the remaining incorporators appoint a new subscriber and re-execute the subscription schedule before payment is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Corporate Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, acting through the InterNet Registry or in-person counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative incorporator or attorney files the complete application for registration of incorporation within the period prescribed by the Commercial Act after completion of capital subscription and payment. The filing package must include the notarized Articles, certified capital subscription and deposit evidence, consent forms of directors and auditor, the corporate seal registration application, and the official court fee receipt. The Registry examiner reviews the company name, legal form, authorized and issued capital, purpose clause, number of shares, office address, officer identities and the method of public notice. Upon acceptance, the Registry records the legal existence of the company, assigns a corporate registration number, and issues the certified corporate registration certificate. The registration date is the company's legal formation date.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription and bank deposit certificates
Consent and appointment documents for directors and auditor
Corporate seal registration application and specimen
Power of attorney and identity evidence of filer
Court filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a request for supplementary explanation, the filer responds in writing through the same registration portal within the stated cure period, supplies the missing notarization or corrected capital statement, or amends the purpose clause; if the application is rejected, a new application and additional fee are required only after the irregularity has been fully cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Tax Invoice Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax online portal and the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after corporate registration, the Representative Director or tax agent files a business registration application with the National Tax Service. The application must identify the company as a Yuhan Hoesa, the registered office address, the business purpose as software publishing, and the relevant tax office. For an electronic content business with in-app payments through Apple and Google, the filer should request electronic tax invoice issuance, VAT registration, and, if foreign shareholders are present, the appropriate withholding tax arrangements. The NTS verifies the corporate registration certificate, lease, identity and legal representative; after approval, it issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the business registration number and assigned tax codes. The certificate is necessary to issue Korean tax invoices and to operate compliantly.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate
Business registration application on the standard NTS form
Copy of Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of corporate seal and representative ID card
Office lease or letter of consent for registered office
Written appointment of tax agent or power of attorney, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS suspends the application pending an address verification, the applicant submits a corrected lease certificate or building owner confirmation; if the business code is contested, the company provides an app description and revenue model to support classification as software publishing; upon resolution, the certificate is issued within the SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Implementation, Bank Account Activation and Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank, local District Court Registry, and Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or KOTRA only for foreign-invested enterprise reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the corporate and business registration certificates, the company convenes the first Board meeting, ratifies this formation dossier, and adopts the pro-forma first board resolution. The authorized directors open the permanent corporate bank account and provide the bank with the corporate registration certificate, business registration number, corporate seal certificate, resolutions and signatory passports. The company then maintains statutory registers, share certificate ledger, board minutes, shareholder registry, and corporate seal book. If any shareholder is non-resident and the FDI notification threshold is met, a foreign investment report must be filed with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or a designated KOTRA center. A tax facilitation number is confirmed for cross-border transactions, and the Apple and Google payment merchant agreements are executed under the authorized representatives.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate
Business registration certificate
First board resolution and minutes
Corporate seal certificate and seal registration card
Identity documents and passports of authorized signatories
Foreign investment report forms only if non-resident investors are present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial ownership information or an out-of-country address proof, the company supplies a certified copy of the shareholders' register and the required self-declaration; if the foreign investment report is rejected, the investor cures the minimum amount or documentation through KOTRA and refiles within the extended time frame.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. The company is a pure digital content publisher and does not require an industrial manufacturing permit. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), official electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); export customs side: Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident that intends to operate through or invest in a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC, the Korean company itself must first complete Korean commercial registry incorporation, then submit the statutory business registration application to the competent NTS district office via HomeTax. The application includes the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, proof of the foreign investor's existence, power of attorney for tax matters, and evidence of the registered place of business in Korea. The NTS assigns a 10-digit Business Registration Number which serves as the taxpayer VAT and corporate tax identifier; the same registration is used for VAT and is mandatory before any taxable supply commences. A foreign non-resident company that has no Korean place of business but makes direct taxable supplies into Korea must separately obtain a VAT business registration for foreign electronic-service suppliers through HomeTax, generally through a domestic tax representative, unless a treaty or NTS published procedure grants exception. No general monetary pre-registration threshold exists; registration is triggered by commencement of business activity or by the making of taxable supplies in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC is a per se domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act; no check-the-box or pass-through election exists. Korean anti-hybrid provisions may apply to mismatches under tax treaties, but no elective classification mechanism is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value Added Tax under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for corporations - registration is mandatory upon commencement of taxable business, regardless of turnover. The only approximate threshold in Korean VAT law is the simplified taxpayer ceiling of KRW 80,000,000 in annual taxable turnover, which applies only to individual entrepreneurs and never to a Yuhan Hoesa LLC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea's NTS operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) regime integrated with HomeTax. VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices for each taxable supply and transmit them to the NTS through HomeTax or an NTS-approved electronic tax invoice service provider; transmission must be completed by the following day after issuance. The NTS system validates transaction data against VAT returns and payment records, and flags mismatches in near real time. There is no blockchain or analogue digital stamping requirement for general software publishers, but app-store/IAP settlements from Apple and Google are reconciliation evidence. For foreign electronic-service suppliers, a simplified electronic VAT filing and e-invoice/upload channel is available via HomeTax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported out of Korea after Korean Customs Service clearance. Services qualify for 0% where they are supplied to a non-resident recipient and are performed or consumed outside Korean territory, including qualifying exported digital content and software-related services, provided the Korean supplier proves that the place of use/benefit lies outside Korea and that the consideration is receivable in foreign currency from abroad. For a Yuhan Hoesa publishing social casino/slots simulations, zero-rating is available only in respect of the offshore supply element - i.e. sales credited to customers located outside Korea or, in B2B chains, services wholly used by non-resident business customers outside Korea. Sales to Korean domestic users through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing remain standard-rated Korean domestic VAT at 10%; the app stores' own VAT/settlement reporting must be reconciled. Export earnings must be collected through authorized Korean foreign-exchange channels by the statutory 180-day deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export declaration processed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system, carrying the export clearance number and zero-rating supporting data
Commercial invoice and, for digital services, a signed service agreement or statement of work identifying the cross-border nature and the non-resident recipient

Bill of lading or air waybill for physical exports; for digital/software exports, offshore download or server usage logs and platform settlement reports from Apple/Google showing foreign end-user purchases
Foreign exchange settlement confirmation issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank evidencing the inward receipt and repatriation of export proceeds in convertible currency
Documents establishing the overseas place of consumption, such as customer billing address, IP address geolocation, tax registration or VAT ID, and end-use certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: During audit, NTS cross-checks zero-rating claims against Korea Customs Service export declarations, foreign-exchange bank settlement records, app-store payout reports, and customer location data. Missing or inconsistent documentation leads to disallowance of the 0% rate and the assessment of 10% VAT on the supply value, plus additional tax penalties and interest under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes. Material false zero-rating or fraudulent refund claims are subject to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, and the NTS may claw back refunds and disallow historical claims within the statutory assessment limitation periods applicable to national taxes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK); foreign exchange administration is jointly governed by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with delegated licensing and reporting executed through foreign exchange banks supervised by the BOK and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized, monitored foreign exchange regime. The Korean won is fully convertible for bona fide current account transactions, including software exports, royalty payments, and profit distributions, subject only to transaction reporting and documentary retention. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity subscription and related-party loans, are generally permitted but require filing through designated foreign exchange banks, and some large or non-bank transactions require advance approval or onboarding to the MOEF reporting system. There is no blanket surrender requirement for export proceeds; Korean exporters must receive export consideration through a licensed foreign exchange bank within statutory timeframes, but they may retain those proceeds in resident foreign currency deposit accounts or convert them to KRW at market rates. For a non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa engaged in digital content monetization via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the key constraint is that every inbound platform payout must be traceable to the entity's registered foreign exchange bank account, with supporting platform settlement statements retained for at least five years. Profit remittance to a foreign parent or shareholder requires certification that corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax have been settled with the National Tax Service; the foreign exchange bank will require the tax payment receipt, financial statements, board resolution approving the dividend, and a beneficial ownership declaration. Overall, South Korea is not a stringent exchange control jurisdiction in the sense of mandatory conversion or central bank rationing, but the administrative burden rests on full reporting, bank intermediation, and documentation to prove the underlying commercial purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Regulations, export proceeds arising from digital services and software publishing must be received through a designated foreign exchange bank within 18 months of the export performance date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio requiring the export proceeds to be changed into KRW; proceeds may be held in a foreign currency account, deposited, or converted at the prevailing market rate. If the 18-month collection deadline is missed, the Yuhan Hoesa must seek an extension through its settlement bank, supported by a documented reason such as ongoing platform payment cycles, legal disputes, or agreed trade credit terms. All inbound wire transfers from Apple and Google must be identified with the correct foreign exchange transaction purpose code and settled in a manner that permits audit trail reconciliation with the platform payout statements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational KRW Currency Account with Ancillary Foreign Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs as principal treasury accounts. South Korean corporate banking, foreign exchange reporting, and KRW clearing are governed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and are serviced only through licensed domestic financial institutions. An offshore EMI such as a digital banking service based in Hong Kong, the EU, or the UK cannot open a fully compliant KRW settlement account for the company without a licensed Korean bank partner, nor can it reliably provide the inward remittance reporting certificate needed for export proceeds and equity capital verification. EMIs may be accepted only as auxiliary non-KRW wallets for developer payouts or contractor disbursements, provided transfer rationale is documented; however, the statutory treasury spine must remain with a Tier-1 Korean bank. Any effort to process Apple or Google IAP outflows through an EMI without direct domestic bank intermediation will likely trigger AML inquiries and audit deficiencies from Korean regulators.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person branch KYC interviews are generally mandatory for at least one registered executive director and each material beneficial owner of a foreign-owned Korean LLC. The CEO or an appointed director with full powers must physically attend a designated foreign exchange bank branch to complete the customer due diligence interview, provide original passports, present the corporate registration certificate, and execute bank signature cards. Remote opening through consular proxy or notarized power of attorney is occasionally accepted by banks with dedicated global corporate desks, but the practice is discretionary, subject to enhanced due diligence, and never automatic. For the Yuhan Hoesa, the offshore shareholder should expect to send its lawful administrator or a locally resident director to the branch; if remote opening is proposed, the bank will require an apostilled power of attorney, certified passports of the ultimate beneficial owner, a recent bank reference, and a notarized certificate of good standing from the shareholder's home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or possible nominee shareholder arrangement because the entity is fully owned by a non-resident and has no operating history in Korea
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete beneficial ownership structure chart down to natural persons, current articles of incorporation, registered director/shareholder registry from the Korean registry court, apostilled passport copies of all beneficial owners, a certificate of incumbency from the home jurisdiction, source of wealth documentation including tax returns and bank statements proving legitimate accumulation of equity capital, and an original bank reference letter for each shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value digital microtransactions from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing creating difficulty in demonstrating that the income originates from bona fide commercial activity rather than layering or third-party proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program agreement, Google Play Developer distribution agreement, at least 12 months of platform payout statements, monthly revenue reconciliation reports from the game operations backend, withholding tax receipts for any commissions paid, annual audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements, and a transaction log matching each platform payout batch to the applicable app store settlement invoice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to overseas software developers and cloud hosting providers that may be misclassified as non-trade payments or disguised repatriations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany or contract master services agreements with defined milestones, line-item invoices from each recipient, evidence of actual service delivery such as hosted code repositories, deployment logs, uptime records, credits from cloud providers, withholding tax certificates if domestic Korean tax was withheld, transfer pricing documentation compliant with the OECD framework, and KYC declarations for every counterparty receiving more than 10,000 USD per month.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reputational and regulatory ambiguity of simulated social casino games appearing as illegal gambling proceeds even if the product has no real-money gambling features
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming that the game is classified as non-real-money social casino content under the Act on Promotion of Game Industry, a copy of the age-gating and responsible gambling disclaimer displayed in the app, the end-user license agreement, a technical attestation that no virtual chips are sellable for real currency and no secondary exchange market exists, platform correspondence confirming Apple and Google classification, and a sanctions and restricted-jurisdiction geoblocking policy showing that the game is not offered in prohibited capital markets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the Korean LLC should be wired by the foreign shareholder via SWIFT MT103 to the foreign exchange bank's collection account, using the investor's registered corporate account and a remittance narrative identifying the payee as the Yuhan Hoesa, the purpose as equity subscription, and the foreign investment intention. The designated foreign exchange bank will file the foreign investment report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) electronic system or the bank's delegated reporting portal. After the inward remittance clears, the bank will issue a foreign exchange purchase certificate and a capital verification confirmation that can be registered with the court for paid-in capital proof. The KRW conversion should be executed at the bank's market rate and credited to the company's domestic operating account. All fees, FX conversion tickets, and reference numbers must be retained for future audits and capital reduction or dividend remittance processes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments should be settled through SWIFT MT103 for royalties, software licenses, contractor fees, cloud infrastructure charges, and intercompany services. MT103 messages must contain the correct Korean foreign exchange purpose code as defined in the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulation, such as the code for software royalties, intellectual property usage, or overseas technical services, and must be supported by underlying invoices and contracts. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are generally unnecessary for digital content distribution because no physical goods move through customs; however, if the entity enters into licensing partnerships that require instrument-based settlement, a stand-by or commercial LC can be issued by the Korean bank against approved documentation such as license certificates and royalty statements. The treasury operation should centralize all disbursement batches in a single banking portal to simplify the outbound trade reporting and reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts for forecasted Apple and Google payout receipts, provided the exposure is supported by actual platform revenue forecasts
Foreign exchange swaps through the designated Korean bank to convert USD receivables into KRW funding without an unhedged open position
Cross-currency swaps where the entity has long-term foreign currency liabilities such as cloud hosting or intercompany loans

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only if executed through the Korean bank's offshore branch or an approved global counterparty and used strictly to hedge KRW exposure in a manner consistent with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act boundaries

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and local corporate income tax surcharge return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax, with the local tax surcharge administered and settled through the same filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, no later than March 31 of the following year; a one-month extension may apply to certain foreign-invested enterprises or when the return is professionally prepared
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Negligence or understatement penalty tax of 20% of the unpaid tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent or manifestly false returns; statutory delinquency interest accrues on overdue amounts; failure to file for three consecutive years or continued dormancy may lead to NTS business-closure disposition, judicial dissolution, and administrative strike-off under the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements, but only when the Yuhan Hoesa crosses the mandatory audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service, Financial Supervisory Service DART filing platform for public registration, and corporate records for the members' annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end for calendar-year entities, ordinarily March 31 of the following year, and no later than the statutory corporate income tax return due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a registered certified public accountant when required is an irregularity under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the company and responsible directors may face administrative fines, prohibition of statutory meeting approvals, and tax assessments based on unaudited accounts may be rejected by the NTS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value added tax preliminary and final returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four annual filing dates for a general VAT taxpayer: January 25, April 25, July 25, and October 25 of the following respective VAT periods; the periods are January-June and July-December with preliminary and final filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional penalty of 20% of the unpaid VAT amount for late or non-filing, 40% for fraudulent reporting, plus daily statutory overdue interest; repeated non-filing can trigger revocation of business registration, attachment of assets, and court-ordered strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual business performance report, if the Yuhan Hoesa has any foreign-invested enterprise status or non-resident ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine may be imposed for late submission or omission; continued non-compliance can result in loss of foreign-invested enterprise status, withdrawal of tax and customs privileges, and a negative filing in subsequent regulatory reviews.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of members of the Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No annual filing to a government registry is required for ordinary meeting minutes; amended articles of organization or changes requiring commercial registration must be filed with the Korean Court Registry within the statutory registration window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year, unless a longer period is approved by judicial authorities; for a calendar-year company, the meeting must be held by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual members' meeting in compliance with the Commercial Act subjects responsible directors and managers to administrative fines, may invalidate the approval of financial statements, and can be used as evidence in an application for judicial dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: No annual business registration renewal is required; business registration status is confirmed through the annual corporate income tax return and the NTS business registration certificate system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation is completed by the corporate income tax filing deadline of March 31 for calendar-year entities; any change in registered items must be reported within 30 days of such change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late change reporting or deliberate non-disclosure may trigger penalty tax, administrative fines, or correction orders; chronic non-filing and dormancy can lead to revocation of the business registration and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered for a Yuhan Hoesa in any of the following situations: (i) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 12,000,000,000; (ii) total assets are at least KRW 7,000,000,000 and the company has an average of 300 or more regular employees in the preceding fiscal year; (iii) the company is a listed company, bond issuer, financial institution, insurer, or is otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission by reason of size, turnover, public interest, or legal mandate; or (iv) another Korean statute or government authority requires audited financial statements for licensing, tax, AML, or regulatory purposes. Entities not satisfying any threshold are treated as small companies and are not statutorily required to engage a certified public accountant, but they must still maintain complete and orderly books and records.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) applies mandatorily to external audit-subject companies and listed entities; a non-audited small Yuhan Hoesa may apply the Korean General Accounting Standards and Simplified Korean SME Accounting Standards, which are aligned with the Korean Commercial Act and Corporate Tax Act for measurement and disclosure purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a standalone annual UBO filing for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa. The company must, however, maintain an accurate member register showing the ultimate natural-person members, update the statutory registers immediately upon any share interest transfer, and report any shareholding transfer to the National Tax Service within 30 days for share transfer tax compliance. If the company is a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any change in foreign ownership or foreign investor particulars must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank within 15 days, and foreign ownership status must be reconfirmed annually through the foreign-invested enterprise annual business performance report. Financial institutions will also require a corporate beneficial ownership attestation under Korean AML rules when bank accounts or payment rails are opened or materially changed.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 18,000 per year, only when the Yuhan Hoesa crosses the mandatory audit threshold; otherwise no statutory audit fee is incurred

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national corporate income tax top bracket plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing an aggregate headline rate of 23.1%; lower national brackets are 9% up to KRW 200,000,000 and 19% up to KRW 20,000,000,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday, no free-zone territorial exemption, and no patent box regime is available in South Korea for an onshore Yuhan Hoesa. Qualifying R&D expenses for software and social gaming content may qualify for a tax credit or super-deduction under the Special Tax Control Treatment Law (STTCL); foreign tax credits are available for foreign-source income. The social-casino/gaming model does not enjoy any industry-specific CIT holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly provisional prepayments for corporations whose prior-year tax exceeded a statutory threshold
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the statutory filing deadline is 31 March of the following year; a one-month extension may be available under the Corporate Tax Act if prior approval is obtained. Provisional payments are due by 31 March for the first half and 31 August for the second half of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and service revenue from social casino, virtual slots, in-app purchases, consumable virtual chips, advertising, and ancillary digital content sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Apple IAP and Google Play Billing revenue in KRW at the standard monthly exchange rate. Non-resident shareholders must not net out dividends or distributions in this box. If foreign platform commissions were paid to non-resident technology intermediaries, commissions are deductible in Box 2 subject to the absence of a Korean permanent establishment and to treaty business-profit attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct service costs, including app-store commissions, payment processing fees, server hosting, licensed game assets, and developer-side content costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to Apple/Google for distribution and payment processing are generally business-profit income of the non-resident, not Korean-source royalties, so no withholding is required if no Korean permanent establishment exists. Intercompany licensed intellectual property fees remain subject to transfer-pricing adjustment and to statutory/treaty withholding tax in later boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit, calculated as Box 1 minus Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that intercompany cost allocations and the arm's length character of commission deductions are supported by contemporaneous documentation; the NTS will recharacterize artificially inflated platform or licensing deductions if the beneficial recipient is a foreign related party.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses: user-acquisition costs, marketing, personnel, legal and compliance, management fees, and royalties paid to related or unrelated licensors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees and royalties paid to a foreign parent or affiliate must satisfy the arm's length standard and must have a documented benefit test. The Korean payer must withhold 22% statutory tax on royalty or service fees unless a tax treaty reduces the rate and the beneficial owner supplies a valid Tax Residency Certificate, corporate status evidence, and a beneficial-ownership declaration before payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating income / taxable income before non-operating items, after book-to-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible entertainment expenses, bribes, fines, and undocumented intercompany charges. Foreign shareholders cannot treat their profit distribution as an expense; profit distribution is an appropriation of after-tax income disclosed in the reconciliation schedule, not a deductible item.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses: interest income, foreign-exchange gains/losses, dividend income, asset impairment, and other non-core items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident shareholder or affiliate is Korean-source and subject to 22% withholding unless reduced by an applicable DTA to 10% to 15%; the beneficial-ownership test applies strictly. Interest income from foreign subsidiaries or deposits must be included in Korean taxable income, with a foreign tax credit claimed in the tax-credit schedule if foreign withholding was suffered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, tax base, current-year income tax after available deductions, tax credits, foreign tax credit, and additional local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident dividend recipients should be reported in the withholding schedule separately. The Korean entity must withhold 22% on dividend distributions to foreign shareholders unless a DTA supplies a lower rate, and must file the prescribed treaty-relief application to the National Tax Service before making a payment. Any treaty-reduced rate is conditional on full economic and legal substance, ownership period, and absence of a conduit arrangement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or underreporting triggers: (i) unfaithful-return penalty up to 20% of unpaid tax; (ii) unfounded-return penalty up to 40% of unpaid tax for evasion through false records; (iii) late-payment surcharge accruing daily at the National Tax Service prescribed interest rate; (iv) criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act if intentional concealment exceeds statutory thresholds, with liquidation penalties, blacklisting, and director liability in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; treaty rates may reduce the dividend withholding rate, commonly to 10% or 15% depending on shareholding size and applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction, execute a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming the recipient is the ultimate beneficial owner and not a conduit, provide corporate existence and shareholding-history evidence, and deliver the completed treaty application to the Korean withholding agent before the dividend payment is made. The withholding agent must submit the application and supporting documents to the National Tax Service in the prescribed electronic/paper format; if tax was withheld at the statutory rate and a lower treaty rate is approved later, the non-resident may file a refund claim with HomeTax, generally within 3 years or the period required by Korean tax procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Korean source withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local income tax surcharge). Under typical Korean tax treaties, arm's length royalties may be reduced to approximately 10% to 15% and interest to approximately 10% to 15%, with the exact rate dependent on the treaty article, limitation-on-benefits provision, and beneficial ownership analysis. The same TRC-and-substance protocol applies before treaty relief can be granted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is required for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 5,000,000,000 in an annual accounting period; Master File preparation is generally required for multinational groups exceeding KRW 100,000,000,000 in consolidated revenue or assets, as adjusted by the International Tax Coordination of Tax Adjustment Act (ITCA) and its Enforcement Decree. Even below the thresholds, a taxpayer must maintain contemporaneous arm's length evidence in response to an NTS adjustment request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the NTS enforces substance-over-form under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the ITCA. A Yuhan Hoesa must demonstrate genuine decision-making, employees, servers, risk-bearing, and operational control in Korea; foreign affiliates must not merely invoice or hold intangible property without performing core income-generating activities. For social casino gaming, CIGA-type substance principles govern whether user contracts, game servicing, and high-value software-development risks are actually borne by the Korean entity, which also underpins DTA beneficial ownership claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised real-money gambling / illegal game operation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating virtual slots or social casino gaming where virtual chips or rewards can be redeemed, transferred, sold, or exchanged for cash, cryptocurrency, gifts, or equivalent monetary value, thereby converting a simulated casual game into an illegal gambling product under Korean criminal and gaming laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Game Industry Promotion Act, illegal game-content production and gambling inducement may be punished by imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 50,000,000; Criminal Act gambling provisions and game-industry administrative orders also apply, with confiscation of illegal proceeds and forced game registration cancellation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize convertible chip ecosystems or secondary-market activities can be criminally prosecuted as principals or co-conspirators, face personal asset seizure/restitution, be named in the Ministry of Culture and NTS blacklisting and travel-restriction system, and may be imprisoned for up to 5 years; the corporate veil will be pierced for fraudulent operation of the legal entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and economic-substance sham
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive royalties, management fees, or platform service fees to a foreign parent or affiliate for intellectual property or services with no actual economic contribution, or failing to prepare and submit the required Local File/Master File covering cross-border transactions with related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may, under the ITCA, recharacterize or disregard non-arm's length transactions and impute income; penalties include up to 30% additional tax on the adjusted underreported income, documented-transaction surcharges, and daily late-payment interest, with criminal referral for willful false apportionment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false transfer-pricing returns or destroy documentation may be held jointly liable for the corporation's unpaid tax under Korean tax statutes, may have their assets attached through secondary collection, may be placed on the NTS delinquent taxpayer blacklist with exit restrictions, and can face imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for deliberate underreporting of corporate income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-resident withholding and dividend tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, or deemed profit distributions to non-resident shareholders or related parties without withholding the statutory rate, without verifying treaty residence/beneficial ownership, or using a false intermediary/architecture to avoid Korean withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes include a 10% additional tax on the withheld amount plus daily late-payment surcharges; intentional evasion or failure to withhold after service of a demand exposes the company to an assessment of the full under-withheld tax, interest, and criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director who causes the company to pay untaxed cross-border distributions becomes a secondary liable person for the unpaid corporate and withholding tax, with personal property collection, travel ban and tax-defaulter blacklisting under the National Tax Collection Act, and imprisonment for up to 5 years or more where the amount evaded is aggravated under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
